findings.summary: A timer2 callback already running is not stopped by cancel(), so the race exists where a timer thread exists. The stated trigger is wrong: threads and solo pools on py-amqp, Redis or SQS use the hub timer on the consumer thread, so on_close and ETA callbacks cannot interleave. The window is otherwise indistinguishable from an ETA task that fired just before the connection loss.

refuting_fact.statement: When the worker uses the event loop the timer is the hub's kombu Timer with no dedicated thread; the timer2 thread is used only without an event loop (Windows, non-asynchronous transports, green pools with their own timer).
refuting_fact.investigator_could_have_seen: Yes, one Read of worker/components.py. Not in the H07 bundle (no occurrence of use_eventloop or timer2).

findings.summary: The facts hold: manual retry() uses a fixed 180 s default delay with no jitter and max_retries=3. The failure story does not follow from them. Retries keep the spread of the original failures shifted by 180 s, nothing compresses them into one moment, and load per wave is still capped by worker concurrency. This is the documented API contract; backoff with jitter is the documented alternative. My judgement on the herd effect is reasoning, not measurement.

refuting_fact.statement: A constant countdown preserves the arrival spread of the failed tasks; it does not synchronise them. The task guide documents retry_backoff and retry_jitter as the pattern for this case.
refuting_fact.investigator_could_have_seen: Partly. The docs are in the repo but .rst files are outside the scan, and the bundle excerpt (865-977) does not even contain the cited lines 842-850. The spread argument needs no file at all.

preconditions.effective_default: jitter has no effect unless retry_backoff is set

missed_defects.description: The database result backend lost its default retries. The code comment and the docs say it defaults to always_retry=True with 3 retries; at runtime it is always_retry=False, max_retries=inf, because conf.get() returns the registered global default. Enabling result_backend_always_retry alone then retries every DatabaseError (including IntegrityError) forever. Established by execution (worker/fr015_defaults.py and my own check on a live app).
missed_defects.why_missed: The investigator read the same two lines and believed the comment. Seeing it needs one executed statement or knowledge of how the settings object resolves defaults. The unit tests also set both values explicitly, so nothing in the repo contradicts the comment.

missed_defects.description: The Reject raised by the dedup fast path is only honoured by the prefork pool. With the solo pool it escapes the tracer and stops the worker ('CRITICAL Unrecoverable error: reject requeue=True'). With the threads pool it is lost in the executor future and the message is never acked or rejected. Established by execution (canvas/fr003_worker.py solo and threads, logs re-read by me).
missed_defects.why_missed: The investigator assumed 'the worker honours exc.requeue' from request.py without tracing how each pool delivers an exception raised outside the task body.

missed_defects.description: Errbacks added with group.link_error() are never dispatched when a chord header fails and the body is that group. group.link_error() stores them on the children and leaves group.options empty, while the handler reads group_callback.options. Established by execution (canvas/fr009_errback.py case 1, healthy broker, nothing published).
missed_defects.why_missed: FR-009 looked at the except block the detector flagged and never checked where the errbacks it iterates come from.

notes: HOW THESE VERDICTS WERE ESTABLISHED. Every 'executed' basis refers to scripts in the session scratchpad (<reviewer-scratchpad>, subdirectories amqp, canvas, redis, worker, review; outputs in rerun/ and review/). Most scripts were written by parallel sub-passes during the first review; for this file I re-ran all of them myself and read the output, and added three new runs (review/recipe_fr001.py, review/real_worker.py in modes timeout, exit, sysexit). Environment: Python 3.12, celery main at 508c112, kombu 5.7.0a1, amqp 5.4.0, billiard 4.3.0, redis-py 8.1.0, SQLAlchemy 2.1.3. No real Redis or RabbitMQ: Redis runs use fakeredis behind a TCP proxy that can refuse or stall; broker runs use the memory transport or mocks; FR-014 used a real PostgreSQL 16.2. Anything depending on real RabbitMQ or SQS behaviour is from reading dependency source and is marked so in each entry. CORRECTIONS TO MY EARLIER PROSE SUMMARY. (1) I said four Verify recipes do not reproduce (FR-001, 005, 006, 009). Running FR-001's recipe literally with fresh threads DOES reproduce its stated outcome, so that claim was wrong for FR-001; it came from a run with warm connections. The accurate list is FR-005 and FR-006 not reproduced, FR-009 non-discriminating (its expected observation occurs with and without the fault, recorded here as not_reproduced), and FR-015 not reproduced on defaults. (2) I said none of the three 'high' findings is correct as written. FR-002's mechanism reproduces exactly on a real worker; its errors are in commit attribution and in which line requeues. I now rate its high as deserved. FR-001 and FR-003 remain over-rated. (3) I said five findings cite commits that neither caused nor corroborate the behaviour (FR-002, 012, 017, 018, 019). Checked with git blame: only FR-012 makes a false claim about its commit, and FR-018's implication is backwards. FR-017 and FR-019 describe their commits accurately; the commits are simply non-corroborating. FR-002's 40c2349 claim is literally true but misses the commit that actually requeues (53dc515). Additional commit errors found now: FR-005 misdates 30402bd ('9 days ago', actually 5). (4) The seven opt-in findings from the summary are FR-002, 003, 007, 010, 011, 012, 018. In this file FR-002, 007, 011, 018 are correct_but_gated; FR-003, 010, 012 are partially_correct because they also contain false claims; their gating is in preconditions. FR-019 needs a user-authored route and is recorded as correct with that precondition. (5) Tally mapping: earlier 9 confirmed = now 5 correct (FR-004, 014, 016, 017, 019) plus 4 correct_but_gated; earlier 10 partial and 2 wrong are unchanged. (6) The three missed defects are the first three entries of missed_defects; two further candidates are listed and flagged as lower certainty. SCHEMA NOTES. The pasted schema was truncated in places. I used: commits.role_actual in {introduced_mechanism, partial_fix_of_same_root_cause, added_the_mitigation, unrelated_change_to_file, other}; detector_leads.verdict in {true_lead, false_lead}; confidence values low|medium|high; why_claimed_was_wrong is null when claimed equals deserved. refuting_fact is null-filled for correct and correct_but_gated findings; their inaccuracies are in summary. location_kind has no value for git history; FR-012's commit-message evidence is filed under scanned_file because a source comment in the cited range says the same thing. wrote_cited_lines comes from git blame -L on every cited code range of the finding. The four uncited leads are attached to one finding of their hotspot for bookkeeping: S04@base.py:773 to FR-007, S19@consumer.py:435 to FR-013, S07 and S19 in database/__init__.py to FR-014.
